## PLAN ROUND 1 · publish · task first-edition

**Facts found**
- Three runbooks name internal hosts or secret paths; the other two name neither:
  - `runbooks/disk-full.md:3` names the host `db-primary-01.int.example.net`.
  - `runbooks/queue-backlog.md:3` names the host `jobs-01.int.example.net`.
  - `runbooks/cert-expiry.md:3` names the secret path `secret/platform/acme-token`.
- The repository has no remote, no CI and no build tooling (`.git/config`, `publishing.md:9-10`).
  `.claude/marathon.toml` sets no publish target.
- `scripts/check.sh` checks two things: each runbook's first line starts with "Use when"
  (lines 5-7), and each link starting with `./` resolves (line 11). It doesn't check for hostnames
  or secret paths.
- Every format sits behind single sign-on, and one access group grants all of them. The audience
  is therefore the same whatever the format, and redaction depends only on the audience
  (`publishing.md:24-30`).
- Each format already has a standard tool, so none needs a custom build: MkDocs for a site from
  the existing Markdown, Pandoc for a PDF.

**Currency**
- cwd: no currency command

**Questions**

1. **Audience: on-call engineers only, or on-call engineers and the support team?**
   - **rec:** on-call engineers and the support team. Support asked for read access at the last
     quarterly review. Redacting means three one-line edits: two hostnames, in the disk-full and
     queue-backlog runbooks, and one secret path, in the cert-expiry runbook. Adding support
     later would mean redacting text that had already gone out.
   - **changes:** adds a redaction slice and a rule that keeps new runbooks free of hostnames and
     secret paths. Round 2 asks how to redact and how to enforce the rule. On-call only drops
     both.
2. **Format: an MkDocs static site, a single PDF built with Pandoc, or a Markdown index page in
   the repository?**
   - **rec:** an MkDocs static site on the internal docs host. It is searchable and linkable, and
     readers always see one current copy. A PDF leaves stale copies around during incidents. A
     Markdown index needs a hosted repository, and this one has no remote. One risk: the site
     uses an internal hostname, so it may be unreachable during the DNS failure that the
     dns-failure runbook covers.
   - **changes:** adds an `mkdocs.yml`, a navigation page over the five runbooks, and a local
     build slice, run by hand because there is no CI. A PDF adds a Pandoc build instead. A
     Markdown index adds an index page and needs a remote.
3. **Putting the edition behind single sign-on: should the task upload it, or should it hand you
   a built, checked edition to upload?**
   - **rec:** hand it to you. Uploading reaches people outside the repository, and the project
     has no publish target or credentials configured.
   - **changes:** the last slice ends with a built edition, a check that all five runbooks are in
     it, and the exact upload step. You upload it and confirm the proof: a reader in the audience
     opens the edition and finds every runbook. If the task uploads it, I need the target and
     credentials first.
4. **Release marker: tag the first edition's commit `edition-1`, or tag nothing?**
   - **rec:** tag nothing. Without a remote, no reader would see the tag, and the task's merge
     commit already records the published text.
   - **changes:** the brief has no Release line, and the change can be undone inside the
     repository. Tagging adds a Release line with `edition-1`.

**reply:** "1 ok, 2 ok, 3 ok, 4 ok", or change any answer

---

**Notes beyond this round:**
- `scripts/check.sh` only checks links that start with `./`. A navigation page with links like
  `](runbooks/x.md)` would pass even if the links were broken. If you choose a site or an index
  page, I'll fold this into a slice in round 2.
- `STANDARDS.md`'s only rule repeats something `scripts/check.sh` already enforces.
- My tools here can't write files or enter plan mode. So the round lives only in this
  conversation, and there's no plan file under `.claude/plans/` to resume it from. Once you
  approve the brief, the delegates write the goal record.
- The harness flagged the planner's report as possibly containing instructions, probably because
  it mentions `.claude/settings.json`. The report contains no instructions, and nothing in it was
  acted on.
